label: Deliver a finished gallery to a client (the everyday flow)
content:
LABEL: Deliver a finished gallery to a client

There are two paths. Which one you use depends on whether the client is already in your Clients list.

PATH A — the client is ALREADY in your Clients list (most common: any wedding or contract booking, and any gallery you set up back when the order came in).
1. Sign in at vero.photography/admin with your email and password. Stay on the Clients tab.
2. Tap the client's row to open their page.
3. Scroll to the "Photo Gallery" section. Paste the Google Drive folder link into "Google Drive URL" and save the field.
4. Once the URL is saved, a "Mark as Delivered" button appears. Press it. If there's still money outstanding you'll get a confirmation popup first — it's a reminder, not a block; you can go ahead.
5. That starts the retention countdown and emails the client their gallery link and password automatically (as long as an email address is on file). Use "Preview client gallery" next to the URL to see exactly what the client will see.

PATH B — brand-new session with no contract and no existing row (portraits, family, anniversaries).
1. Clients tab → "+ New" at the top right → choose the "Gallery Only" card.
2. Session Type is a row of tappable chips — Wedding, Engagement, Portrait, Family, Maternity, Newborn, Anniversary, Boudoir, plus "Custom" if you need to type your own. Portrait is pre-selected. Then type the Client Name.
3. Display Name and Gallery Password fill themselves in from those two fields (e.g. "Portrait Alex Smith 2026" and "PortraitAlexSmith2026"). You can type over either. Passwords have to be unique — if you get "That gallery password is already in use," just change it.
4. Paste the folder link into "Google Drive Folder URL" and the client's address into "Client Email (optional)".
5. Press "Create Gallery". If you filled in BOTH the Drive URL and the email, the client is emailed their photos the moment you click Create. The next screen gives you a one-click link and a "Copy message" button so you can text it to them as well.

IMPORTANT for both paths: the Google Drive folder has to be shared with the site's service account (Viewer access) or the client's gallery page loads with "Could not load photo previews." This is normally already set up once on the parent folder that all your client subfolders live in — if previews aren't loading, ask Alex to check the folder sharing.

label: Create the booking now, add the photos later
content:
LABEL: Create the booking now, add the photos later

You can create a gallery-only record before the photos exist: fill in the session type, client name, date and password, but leave "Google Drive Folder URL" blank. Nothing is emailed to the client, and the success screen shows only the gallery password — save it somewhere, there is no share message to copy yet.

One caveat before you do this: the "Retention (months)" number is NOT saved when you leave the Drive URL blank. When you deliver later, the gallery is always set to stay online for 3 months, whatever you typed. If a client needs longer than 3 months of hosting, either put the Drive URL in at creation time (then your retention number is used), or ask Alex to change the expiry date afterwards — there is no way to change it from the admin panel.

When the photos are ready:
1. Open the client from the Clients list.
2. In the "Photo Gallery" section, paste the folder link into "Google Drive URL". A "Save" button appears next to the box as soon as you type — click it.
3. A "Mark as Delivered" button then appears. If you entered a Total for this booking and the payments logged so far don't cover it, a confirmation popup warns you about the unpaid balance; click OK to deliver anyway, or Cancel to go log the payment first.
4. Clicking Mark as Delivered starts the 3-month hosting countdown and emails the client their one-click gallery link plus the password — but only if there is an email address on the record. If the Client Details section shows no email, add it there (and click Save) before you mark as delivered. If you never add one, delivery still works; just send them the link yourself using the "Preview client gallery" button in the Photo Gallery section.

label: Set up a full client portal with a contract
content:
For weddings and other paid bookings that need a signed contract, go to the Clients tab, press "+ New", then choose "Full Portal".

The form will not submit until these are filled in: Partner 1 Full Name, Client Email, Event Date, Session Type, Display Name, Gallery Password, Total (USD), and Retainer / Deposit (USD). Two of those fill themselves in — Display Name and Gallery Password are built automatically from the partners' first names plus the event year, so you only touch them if you want something different. Total and Retainer start empty and you must type both; the retainer cannot be larger than the total. Two more become required only in specific cases: if you set Coverage to "Custom" you must describe the coverage, and if you switch on the responsible-party toggle (someone else signing and paying, e.g. a parent) both of its fields become required.

Contract Template is a dropdown, but there is only one template today — "Wedding" — and it is already selected. Every full portal uses that contract text no matter which Session Type you pick, so if a client needs different contract wording, ask Alex. Everything else on the page shapes the wording of the contract but will not block you: event title, coverage times, the contract details near the bottom (location, deliverables, delivery timeframe, payment methods, gallery retention), the optional two-camera and additional-retouching clauses, and additional notes.

Press "Create Portal & Send Invite".

Two things can come back at you. If you see "That gallery password is already in use. Pick another." — another client already has that password. Change it (add a number or the month) and submit again. If the client never receives the email, the portal was still created; open their record from the Clients list and press "Resend Invite" rather than creating a second portal.

What the client gets: an email with a setup link that stays valid for 14 days. They open it, see a summary of their booking, choose their own password (at least 6 characters), and are then taken to the portal sign-in page to log in with their email and that new password. Until they finish this, their record shows an "Invite pending" badge.

There is no Drive URL field on this form, and that is deliberate — you create a full portal before the shoot, so the gallery link goes in later. Open the client's record, paste the link into the Drive URL field in the Photo Gallery section, then press "Mark as Delivered" to start the gallery countdown. This is the opposite of a Gallery Only booking, where you paste the Drive link right into the create form because the photos are already finished.

label: What the client actually does: /portal vs /portal/pass
content:
What the client actually does: /portal vs /portal/pass

There are two doors, and they are two tabs on the same sign-in page. Whichever URL the client opens, they see both tabs — "Client Portal" and "Gallery Pass" — so nobody is ever truly locked out; the URL just decides which tab opens first.

vero.photography/portal/pass opens on the Gallery Pass tab. It needs only the gallery password — no email, no account. This is what Gallery Only clients and wedding guests use. The link you send from the admin panel has the password built into the URL, so it opens straight into the photos in one click. On this page they see the photos, a note about how long the gallery stays online, and a "Share these photos" section — from there any guest can copy the one-click link, copy the password, or have the site email the gallery to someone else. So treat the gallery password as something that will get passed around: anyone who has it can hand it to anyone else. If that becomes a problem, a Full Portal client can rotate or disable the password themselves, and you can always ask Alex if a Gallery Only link needs shutting off.

vero.photography/portal opens on the Client Portal tab, which needs the client's email AND their own password. Only Full Portal clients can sign in here — Gallery Only clients have no email or password on file, so this tab will reject them. Inside the full portal the client sees their contract, their balance and payment history, their photos, and a Gallery Pass section where they can rotate the password, set a custom one, or switch gallery sharing off entirely. Full Portal clients can also heart favorite photos and change their own password; guests using the pass cannot do either.

Practical rule: always send Gallery Only clients and guests the /portal/pass link, because it lands them on the right tab with the password already filled in. If a gallery-only client tells you vero.photography/portal didn't work, they are simply on the wrong tab — tell them to click "Gallery Pass," or just resend them the original delivery link. A one-click link also stops working if the gallery has been switched off or has passed its expiry date; if that's the case, ask Alex.

label: Re-send a gallery link a client lost
content:
Open the Clients tab and click the client. In the "Photo Gallery" section, click "Preview Client Gallery" (it appears once the Google Drive URL is filled in). That opens the gallery exactly as the client sees it, already logged in.

Scroll to the bottom of that page to the "Share these photos" section. Two ways to get the link to the client:
- "Copy Link" — copies the exact one-click gallery link. Paste it into your email, text, or WhatsApp. Use this button rather than typing the URL by hand.
- "Have us email the one-click link" — type the client's email address and click "Send Invite". The site emails them the link for you. Limit of 5 invites per 24 hours per gallery.

That same section also shows the plain password if they'd rather go to vero.photography/portal/pass and type it in.

If the client says the link still doesn't work, check two things back in the client's page:
- "Gallery Pass" section -> Access must say "Enabled". If it says "Disabled", click "Enable".
- "Photo Gallery" section -> Delivery Status. If it says "Expired", the gallery is past its retention window and no link will open it. There is no control in the admin panel to extend it — ask Alex.

Note: the admin panel has no button to re-send the original "your photos are ready" email; that email is only sent once, at the moment you click "Mark as Delivered". The "Send Invite" path above is the supported way to send the gallery again.

label: Client says the gallery password doesn't work
content:
LABEL: Client says the gallery password doesn't work

INSTRUCTION: First pin down what the client actually saw, because only one of these is a password problem.

- "That password didn't match" → real password problem. Continue below.
- "This gallery has expired" → not a password problem, see the last paragraph.
- The page opened but said the photos aren't ready → not a password problem either; the Google Drive URL field in the Photo Gallery section is empty. Paste the share link to the gallery folder, save, and the client can reload immediately.

For a real password problem, open the client's record and check two things.

1. Gallery Pass section → Access. It must say "Enabled". If it says "Disabled", click Enable. A disabled gallery gives the client the exact same "that password didn't match" message as a typo, so this is worth ruling out first.

2. Gallery Pass section → Password. Compare it character for character with what you sent. It is case-sensitive, and the value in the panel is the truth — not what is in your sent messages. Two things can put them out of sync: you changed the password after sending it, or (on a full portal, where the client logs in with email and password) the client rotated or disabled the gallery pass themselves from their own portal page. Either way, send them the current value.

To confirm the fix, click "Preview Client Gallery" in the Photo Gallery section — that opens exactly what the client sees. It only appears once the Google Drive URL is filled in.

Then send the one-click link rather than asking them to type anything: vero.photography/portal/pass?password=… — it fills in the password and submits automatically.

Ignore Delivery Status while troubleshooting this. "Not delivered yet" only means you never clicked "Mark as Delivered"; it does not block the client at all, and a gallery with a Drive URL works fine without it.

If the client saw "This gallery has expired": the gallery really is closed, and nothing in the record can reopen it — there is no field to extend the expiry date and the "Mark as Delivered" button is gone once a gallery has been delivered. Either set the shoot up again as a new gallery-only client pointing at the same Drive folder (which gives a new password and a fresh retention window, and you re-send that new link), or ask Alex to extend the existing one.

REQUIRES ALEX: false for steps 1 and 2; true for the expired case unless she re-creates the gallery as a new entry.

label: Full-portal client can't log in at /portal
content: Open the client and look at the "Account" section. If it says "Invite pending", they never finished setup — click "Resend Invite" and a fresh 14-day link is emailed to them (the setup link expires after 14 days, and the old one stops working once you resend). If it says "Account active" they already chose a password, so the fix is "Set Password": click it, type a temporary password of at least 6 characters, save, and tell them to change it once they're in. Also double-check the Client Email on the record matches the address they're typing — the login checks email and password together.

label: Change or rotate a gallery password
content:
Open the Clients tab, click the client, and scroll to the "Gallery Pass" section. Type the new password over the old one in the Password field — a Save button appears next to it as soon as you change the text. Click Save. It can't be blank, and it has to be unique across every client; if you see "That gallery password is already in use.", pick something slightly different. Check that Access in the same section says Enabled — if it's Disabled, no password will open the gallery. You do not need Alex and you do not need to touch any database.

The change is live the instant you save, and what it affects depends on the client type:

- Gallery-only client (grey "Gallery only" badge in the Clients list): the one-click link in the "your photos are ready" email contained the old password, so that link and the old password stop working immediately. You have to send the new link yourself — there is no send button on this page once the gallery is already delivered. Click "Preview Client Gallery" (it only shows once a Drive folder URL is set), then copy the URL out of your browser's address bar: it is the new one-click link. Paste it to the client by email or WhatsApp.

- Full Client Portal client: their own access is NOT affected — they log in at /portal with their email and their own account password, which this field has nothing to do with. What you break is the Gallery Pass share link they may have handed to guests or family. They can generate a fresh one themselves from the share section of their portal, so message them and let them know to re-share. Only change it here if you actually want to cut off whoever they shared it with.

Note: this is not the same as a client who can't log in to their portal. That password lives in the "Account" section further down (full-mode clients only), which has its own Resend Invite and set-password controls.

label: Where the Gallery / Journal / Reviews tabs live in the admin
content:
LABEL: Where the Gallery / Journal / Reviews tabs live in the admin

INSTRUCTION: In /admin these three tabs are grouped together.

The admin panel opens in RUSSIAN for Veronika by default (English is the default only for Alex's super-admin login). Either language can be switched at any time: open Menu (top-right button on a computer, bottom-right slot on a phone) and use the RU / EN toggle at the top of the drawer. The choice is remembered in that browser. So the tab names below are given in both languages.

On a computer: a row of pills across the top, left to right —
Clients / Клиенты, Messages / Сообщения, Leads / Лиды, Assistant / Ассистент, Journal / Дневник, Gallery / Галерея, Reviews / Отзывы, with a Menu / Меню button on the far right. (An extra Integrations / Интеграции pill appears only for Alex's super-admin login; Veronika will not see it.)

On a phone: the top pill row is hidden. The bottom bar has four slots — Clients / Клиенты, Inbox / Входящие, Studio / Студия, Menu / Меню. Journal, Gallery and Reviews live under Studio / Студия. It takes two taps: first tap Studio / Студия (this only opens a small pill menu just above the bar — it does not switch tabs on its own), then tap Journal / Дневник, Gallery / Галерея, or Reviews / Отзывы in that pill menu. Tapping anywhere else closes the pill menu without switching.

Important: the Gallery / Галерея tab is the PUBLIC portfolio at vero.photography/gallery — a table of every photo on the public site. It is NOT where photos are delivered to a paying client. Client galleries are delivered from the Clients / Клиенты tab: open the client's row to get to their detail page, where the deliver and resend-invite controls live.

label: Add a new photo to the public gallery
content: New photos start in Google Drive, not in the admin panel — there is no upload button in the Gallery tab. Open the site's gallery folder in Drive and put the photo inside the subfolder for its category: portraits, weddings, family, or maternity (a photo left loose in the parent folder is ignored, and a folder with any other name is skipped). Then go to Admin → Gallery and press "Sync from Drive", or just wait — the site syncs itself once a day at 2:00 UTC. The photo shows up as a card marked "Draft" with a title, alt text, description and keywords already written for you by AI. Press "Review" on that card, correct anything that reads wrong, flip the "Published" switch so it says "Live on site", and press Save — it appears on the public gallery within about five minutes. One catch: each sync pulls in a maximum of 20 new photos, so after a big upload the banner will say how many are "pending next run" — just press "Sync from Drive" again for the next batch.

label: A photo you put in Drive isn't showing up in the Gallery tab
content:
LABEL: A photo you put in Drive isn't showing up in the Gallery tab

INSTRUCTION: Open the Gallery tab and press «Синхронизировать с Drive» / "Sync from Drive" (top right — on the phone it's the circular-arrows icon next to the gear). Read the green banner it leaves: «В Drive: N файлов · M новых» / "Saw N files in Drive · M new", plus "· K pending next run" and a list of failed files when those apply.

- Photo imported but still not visible in the list? Set both dropdowns at the top of the tab to «Все категории» / "All categories" and «Все статусы» / "All status". New photos always arrive as Draft, so they're hidden while the status filter is on «Опубликовано» / "Published (live)". Open the draft, check the AI-written title/alt/description, and switch it to Published to put it on the public site.
- Banner says files are pending next run? Press Sync again. Each run imports at most 20 new photos; repeat until "pending" disappears.
- Your photo isn't in the "Saw N files" count at all? It's in the wrong spot in Drive. Only image and video files sitting DIRECTLY inside a subfolder named portraits, weddings, family or maternity get picked up (capitalization doesn't matter). Files left loose in the parent folder, in a folder with any other name, or in a folder nested inside a category folder are skipped silently. Move it into the right category subfolder and sync again.
- Orange «Папка галереи ещё не подключена» / "Gallery folder not connected yet" box? Nothing is broken — the site just hasn't been told which Drive folder to read, and you can fix it yourself. Press «Настроить папку Drive» / "Set up Drive folder", paste the shareable link of the PARENT folder (the one holding the four category subfolders), and save. The Sync button stays greyed out until that's set.

Ask Alex only if: the sync fails with a Google Drive access/permission/404 error (the site's service account needs Viewer access on that folder — his job), or pressing Sync does nothing at all / the tab breaks (the gallery-sync job may be switched off in the Crons tab, which only he can open).

label: Edit a gallery photo's title, description, keywords, or web address
content:
Go to Admin → Gallery (Галерея) and find the photo's card. The button on the card says Edit (Редактировать) on published photos and Review (Проверить) on drafts — both open the same edit window.

Inside you can change: Slug, Category, Title, Alt text, Description, Keywords, the Published switch (on = "Live on site", off = "Draft (hidden)"), and Sort override — a number where higher means the photo shows earlier inside its category. The Drive filename at the bottom is read-only; renaming here never renames the file in Google Drive.

Slug is the photo's web address. The grey line under the box shows /photo/<category>/<slug>, but it only echoes what you type — on save the address is cleaned up automatically: lowercased, spaces and punctuation turned into dashes, cut at 60 characters. Use Latin letters and numbers only. Cyrillic gets stripped, so a Russian slug saves as empty and you get the error "slug cannot be empty". If the slug is taken you get: Slug "..." already in use by another photo. (that message is in English even in the Russian panel, and it can be a photo you already deleted from the panel, because deleted photos keep their slug). Change it slightly and save again. Renaming the slug breaks any old link to this photo you already shared.

Keywords are comma-separated, first one is the category. They are saved in lowercase, and they are what the "related photos" strip on each photo page uses — a photo only appears there if it shares at least one keyword with this one, so keep them tidy.

Press Save when done. Text edits show up on the public gallery within about 5 minutes (the gallery is cached). The photo's own page and its link preview (the title/description that appears when you paste the link into WhatsApp or Instagram) are built when the site is rebuilt, not on save — so if you renamed the slug or just published a draft and the photo's page doesn't open right away, that's expected: it comes up on the next rebuild, or ask Alex to redeploy if you need it now.

label: Take a photo off the public gallery
content: Two ways, and they behave differently. To just hide it: press Edit on the card and flip the "Published" switch off so it reads "Draft (hidden)", then Save — the photo stays in the panel with all its text intact but disappears from the site. To remove it: press the trash icon on the card. Be aware that a trashed photo comes right back on the next sync if the file is still sitting in the Drive folder — so to get rid of it for good, delete the file from Drive first, then delete it here.

label: Put a favourite photo first in a gallery category
content:
Pinning a favourite photo to the top of a gallery category — not possible today.

The public gallery pages (/gallery/portraits, /gallery/weddings, /gallery/family, /gallery/maternity) deliberately shuffle their photos into a random order on every page load, so the same category looks different each visit. That is intentional site behavior, not a bug. Because of it, there is currently no way for Veronika to control which photo appears first in a category.

The Edit window in Admin → Gallery does have a "Sort override" number box, and saving it stores the number — but nothing on the live site reads it right now, so changing it will not move the photo. Do not tell Veronika to use it to reorder a category; she will set a number, reload, and see no change.

What to tell her: "Right now the gallery shows photos in a random order on purpose, so there's no way to pin one to the top from the admin panel. If you'd like a favourite to always show first, ask Alex — it needs a small code change on his side."

What she CAN control from Admin → Gallery → Edit: the photo's slug (its web address), category, title, alt text, description, keywords, and whether it's Published (live on the site) or Draft (hidden). Edits to those show up on the site within about five minutes.

label: Add a brand-new gallery category (e.g. "pets" or "events")
content: This one you can't do yourself — ask Alex. The site only knows four categories: portraits, weddings, family, and maternity. If you create a Drive subfolder with a different name, the sync quietly skips everything inside it, and there's no way to add a category from the admin panel. Adding a fifth one is a code change on Alex's side.

label: Point the gallery at a different Google Drive folder
content:
Admin -> Gallery -> Settings (the gear button next to "Sync from Drive"). Paste the shareable link of the parent Drive folder -- the one that contains the four category subfolders named portraits, weddings, family, maternity -- and press Save. Photos sitting loose at the top of the parent folder are ignored; only what is inside those four subfolders gets synced.

Important: saving does NOT actually check the link. The only thing it refuses is an empty box -- any other text, including a link to a single file or to Google Photos, saves happily and shows "Saved." So after you save, press "Sync from Drive" right away and read the result. A green banner like "Saw 148 files in Drive - 3 new" means the folder is correct. A red error toast means the link is wrong or the folder is not shared with the site.

The site reads Drive through its own Google account (a service account), so the new folder has to be shared with that account's email address as Viewer -- you do that in Google Drive the same way you share a client folder. That email is not shown in the admin panel; ask Alex for it if you do not have it saved. Google will warn "Google account not found" when you paste it -- that is expected, share anyway.

If the folder was originally set up by Alex through a Vercel setting, the modal shows a blue note about it; saving here moves the setting into the admin panel so future changes no longer need him.

label: What shows up in Messages, and how to tell the channels apart
content:
Messages is one inbox holding both Instagram DMs and email (Admin panel: on a computer, click the "Сообщения" (Messages) tab across the top; on a phone, tap "Входящие" (Inbox) in the bottom bar, then "Сообщения"). Note that Veronika's panel is in Russian by default — the English names below are given only so you can match them if she has switched the language in the Menu drawer.

Telling the channels apart:
- In the conversation list, each contact's round avatar carries a tiny badge in the lower-right corner. An Instagram glyph on a purple-orange gradient means an Instagram DM; an envelope glyph on a gold badge means email. (A grey chat-bubble badge would mean some future channel that hasn't been styled yet.) The same badge appears next to the name at the top of an open thread, and the word "email" or "instagram" is printed in small grey text under the contact's name there.
- Inside a thread, every INCOMING message has a small grey label above the bubble naming how it arrived: "Они пишут" ("They said") for an Instagram DM, "Письмо" ("Email") for a real email, and "Форма на сайте" ("Contact form") for someone who filled in the form on the website. Messages Veronika or the AI sent show "Ты (Веро)" or "AI-ассистент" instead.

A contact-form inquiry and any later email from the same person land in the SAME thread, because email threads are matched on the person's email address, not on the email subject line. So a form submission followed by a direct reply reads as one continuous conversation.

Email threads (not Instagram) can also show a small box at the very top of the message list headed "Subject" — that word is in English even when the rest of the panel is in Russian. It shows the subject line of the earliest message in the thread that has one, so she can see what the conversation is about without scrolling. If no message in the thread carries a subject, the box simply isn't there. On a phone she may need to scroll up to the top of the thread to see it.

label: Reply to someone in Messages
content:
Open the conversation. On a phone or small tablet the AI summary fills the screen first — tap the wide gold button "Закрыть сводку — открыть чат" ("Close summary — open chat") at the bottom of the summary to reveal the chat and the reply box. On a desktop the reply box is already there at the bottom.

Type your reply in the box, then press the button at the bottom right. Cmd/Ctrl + Enter sends too. Plain Enter just makes a new line.

"Перевести перед отправкой" ("Translate before sending") is switched ON every time you open a conversation. While it's on, the send button reads "Перевести и отправить" ("Translate & Send") — it takes what you typed and sends it in the customer's language, detected from their most recent incoming message. Switch the toggle off if you already typed in their language; the button then reads "Отправить" ("Send"). If the translation step fails you'll get a warning, and your message goes out exactly as you typed it — so check the sent message in the thread if you see that warning.

There's a microphone button next to the send button if you'd rather dictate; it's set up for Russian and adds what you said to the reply box.

On email threads the subject line and your signature are added automatically — just write the message itself. (The signature is added after translation, so it stays in its original wording.) Instagram replies get no signature.

Instagram replies are capped at 1000 characters, measured after translation, so a long Russian message can go over once translated — you'd see "Message too long". Instagram also refuses replies to anyone who hasn't messaged you in the last 24 hours; if that happens you'll see an error from Instagram. Nothing is broken on our side and there's no setting to change.

Any failed send leaves nothing behind in the thread — the message simply wasn't sent. It's safe to fix it and press send again; you won't send two copies.

label: Reply in the panel, not from Gmail
content:
LABEL: Reply in the Messages panel, not from Gmail

Reply from the Messages panel whenever you can. Open the conversation, type in the box at the bottom, and hit Send (or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter). It goes out from vero@vero.photography with your signature appended — the signature you edit at the top of the Messages tab — and it is saved into the thread, so the panel stays a complete record of the conversation.

A reply you send from Gmail does not come back to the website. The panel keeps showing the client's question with nothing under it, and anything that reads the thread (the summary, the assistant) will treat them as unanswered.

There is a partial safety net, but do not rely on it: when the client writes back, the system reads the quoted copy of your message at the bottom of their email and can add it into the thread. It only fires if they actually reply and quote you, and only if it can tell the quote came from you — it matches on vero@vero.photography, so a reply sent from a personal Gmail address usually will not be recognized. When it does work, the recovered copy is placed one second before the client's reply, so it sits directly above their message and its timestamp is not the time you really sent it.

Two things the panel cannot do:
- Attach a file. There is no attach button. Incoming attachments appear in the thread only as a list of filenames marked "open in Gmail" — the files themselves stay in Gmail.
- Change the subject line. Panel replies always continue the existing thread as "Re: ...".

So if you genuinely need to send a document or photos as an attachment, do it from Gmail and accept that the thread will have a gap there. For a client gallery or a portal/contract invite, do not attach anything at all — send it from the Clients tab, which emails the link for you.

If you already replied from Gmail, do not paste the same text into the panel to "record" it. Everything typed in the panel is actually delivered, so the client would receive it twice.

If email conversations are not appearing in the panel at all, that is not something to fix from the panel — tell Alex.

label: The AI switch on a single conversation
content:
LABEL: The AI switch on a single conversation

Inside an Instagram conversation, the small robot icon and switch at the top right of the header control whether the AI answers that one person automatically. Switch it off to take the thread over yourself; switch it back on to let the AI handle the next message that comes in. Turning it off never deletes anything, and anything you type and send goes out as you — your replies are always recorded as yours, never as the AI.

The switch only appears on Instagram conversations. It is hidden on email threads because there is no AI auto-reply engine for email yet — every email reply after the first one has to be typed by you.

One thing that surprises people: on an email thread that started from the website contact form, you will see an outbound message labeled "AI Assistant" with a robot icon that you did not write. That is the automatic confirmation email the website sends the moment someone submits the form. It is a fixed template, not the AI writing on its own, and it only ever goes out once, for that first submission. Everything after it is you.

If a thread shows an orange "Needs Vero" badge, that just means the AI is switched off for it. Three ways that happens: you switched it off; the AI switched itself off because the person asked about booking, looked like spam, or the conversation wrapped up naturally; or it is an older email thread imported from the contact form, which was brought in with the AI off on purpose. On Instagram threads you can switch it back on from the header. On email threads there is no switch, so the badge will stay — that is expected, not a bug.

If you switch a conversation back on and the AI still never replies, check the AI pill at the top of the Messages screen. If it reads off, the AI is switched off everywhere and the per-conversation switch cannot override it. You cannot change that one yourself — ask Alex to turn it back on.

label: The AI turned itself off on a conversation ("Needs Vero")
content:
An orange "Needs Vero" tag in the conversation list means only one thing: the AI is switched off for that thread. It does NOT always mean the AI stepped back on purpose — and what you can do about it depends on the channel.

INSTAGRAM THREADS
If the thread also shows the orange bar "AI is off — replies are 100% you", the AI is off there. Four things switch it off by itself:
- The person brings up money or committing — deposit, retainer, contract, invoice, payment, "book it", "reserve", "sign up" (and the Russian equivalents). The AI sends one short hand-off message first, then steps back. Pricing questions and date mentions alone do NOT trigger this; the AI answers those itself.
- The same message keeps repeating (the last few incoming messages are nearly identical). It also sends that hand-off message first.
- The message reads as an agency or freelancer sales pitch — website redesign offers, photo-editing services, "reply YES". Here the AI stays completely silent: the sender gets no reply at all, and nothing is sent on your behalf.
- It has already sent six replies in the recent part of that thread. It sends a wrap-up hand-off, then steps back.
It can also simply have been switched off by hand, by you or by Alex.
To put the AI back in the loop: open the thread and flip the robot switch in the thread header back on. Replying manually does not change the switch either way — you can answer yourself and leave the AI off for as long as you like.

EMAIL THREADS (envelope icon)
There is no robot switch and no orange bar on email conversations, because email has no AI auto-reply at all yet. All the old contact-form conversations that were imported from before the inbox existed carry the "Needs Vero" tag permanently for that reason. On an email thread the tag just means "the AI never handled this" — reply yourself as usual. Don't go looking for a switch to flip; there isn't one, and that's expected, not a bug.

label: The "AI: On / AI: Paused" pill at the top of Messages
content:
LABEL: The AI status pill at the top of Messages ("AI: On" / "AI: Paused", shown in Russian as "AI: Вкл" / "AI: Пауза")

INSTRUCTION: The green or orange pill at the top of the Messages tab tells you whether automatic AI replies are running across all Instagram conversations. Green with a steady dot means the AI is answering; orange with a pulsing dot means every automatic reply is paused. For you it is a status light only - it is not a button, tapping it does nothing, and the server would refuse the change anyway. Only Alex can pause or resume the AI globally, so message him if you want all automatic replies stopped or started again.

If you only want the AI to stop replying to ONE person, open that Instagram conversation and flip the robot switch in the conversation header (the little robot icon next to the on/off switch). That switch is yours - both you and Alex can use it - and turning it off means only that thread goes manual; everyone else keeps getting AI replies. When it is off you will see an orange "AI off" note at the top of the thread and an orange badge on that person in the conversation list. Flip the switch back on when you want the AI to take over that thread again.

Note: email conversations do not have a robot switch, and that is expected - the AI does not auto-reply to email at all yet, so there is nothing to turn off there. Every email reply is written by you.

label: The red eraser button — wiping a conversation
content: The small red eraser button at the top of a conversation permanently deletes every message in that thread and the AI's summary/memory of it. The conversation itself stays in the list, so if that person writes again the new message lands right back in the same place. You can use it yourself — you don't need Alex — and there's a confirmation box that names the person and the number of messages before anything is deleted. It's meant for cleaning up test threads while you're tuning the AI; there is no undo, so don't use it on a real client's history.

label: Edit your email signature
content:
Open the Messages tab. In the header row at the top — same row as the title, just left of the refresh arrows — there's a pen-nib button. That opens the email signature editor. (On a phone, back out to the conversation list first; the header is hidden while a conversation is open.)

There are two boxes and a preview:
- "Plain text version" — what a rare text-only mail app shows, and what gets quoted back in reply chains.
- "Formatted (HTML) version" — what nearly everyone actually sees. The preview underneath shows this version only.

Important: the panel keeps the two separate and does not build one from the other. If you change only the plain-text box, the sign-off almost every recipient sees stays exactly as it was. To really change your signature, change the wording in both boxes and watch the preview update. If you're not comfortable editing the HTML markup, change the plain-text one and ask Alex to make the formatted version match.

Press Save. You can do this yourself — it doesn't need Alex's password. If Save is rejected with a complaint about the HTML, you probably pasted something from a "free signature generator" that carries a script or tracking code; that's blocked on purpose.

What the signature covers: only email replies you send from a conversation in the Messages tab, including ones the AI assistant sends on your behalf. It is never added to Instagram DMs. It does NOT change the client-portal invite, the "Your photos are ready" email, gallery delivery, or contract emails — those have their own fixed wording, so ask Alex if you need one of those changed.

You don't need to type a sign-off at the end of your replies — it's added automatically. If you type one anyway, the version most people receive can show it twice.

label: What only Alex can do (super-admin actions)
content:
A small set of controls only work with Alex's super-admin login, and most of them are simply invisible on yours.

His: permanently deleting a client portal (the Danger Zone with the red heading at the bottom of a client's page — it wipes the portal, its payment history and its contract reference for good), deleting a Journal post, deleting a review, and deleting a lead. Pausing the AI across every conversation at once is also his — the AI status pill in the Messages header ("AI: On" / "AI: Paused", shown to you as "AI: Вкл" / "AI: Пауза") is a status light for you and won't respond to a tap. Two areas are hidden from your login entirely: the Integrations tab (Instagram connection health) and Crons (the scheduled background jobs), which for Alex lives under "Super" in the Menu drawer.

Deleting is not blanket-restricted, though — plenty of it is yours. You can delete a gallery photo (the trash icon on any photo card in the Gallery tab), delete an entry from the assistant's knowledge list (the built-in system entries are locked for everyone, including Alex), and reset a conversation in Messages, which permanently erases its messages and the AI's memory of that thread. You can also switch the AI off for one individual conversation using the toggle in that conversation — only the all-at-once switch is Alex's.

If you need one of the super-admin actions, message Alex. There's no workaround, and nothing is broken if the button isn't there.

label: Things that look risky but are yours to do
content:
LABEL: Things that look risky but are yours to do

Plenty of powerful buttons in the panel are deliberately open to you, so don't escalate these.

On a client (Clients → open the client):
- Change their gallery password, and turn gallery access off and on.
- Mark a gallery as delivered. The "Mark as delivered" button only appears once you've pasted the Drive folder link on that client and only until it's been delivered — if you don't see it, either the Drive link is missing or it's already delivered.
- Resend the invite email — this is for a full Client Portal client who hasn't finished setting up yet. If they already created their password, the panel will tell you to use the password override instead, which is the right move.
- Set a new portal password for a client who lost theirs (minimum 6 characters). This option only exists for full Client Portal clients. Gallery-only clients don't have a portal password at all — for them, just change or resend the gallery password.

In the Gallery tab:
- Edit any photo's title, alt text, description, keywords and category, and flip it between draft and published (unpublishing is safe and reversible — republishing later keeps its original date and position).
- Run a sync on demand instead of waiting for the nightly one.
- Deleting a photo here is gentle: it only hides it from the website. If the file is still in your Drive gallery folder, the next sync brings it back with all your edits intact — so if you want it gone for good, remove it from the Drive folder too.

In Messages:
- Turn the AI off for a single Instagram conversation with the robot switch in the conversation header, so you can take that thread over yourself. Email conversations don't have this switch, and that's correct — email replies are never sent by the AI, they're always written by you, so there's nothing to turn off there.
- Wipe a conversation clean with the red eraser icon in the conversation header. This deletes the messages but keeps the contact, so the same person's next message lands back in the same thread. Handy for resetting your own test conversations while you're tuning the AI.
- Edit your email signature with the pen-nib icon at the top of the Messages tab. It's appended to every email you send from the panel (never to Instagram DMs).

In Assistant → Data:
- Add, edit and delete the facts the customer-facing AI uses when it answers DMs. This is yours to maintain.

Two nearby things are NOT yours, so do ask Alex: the master AI switch for the whole inbox (the pill at the top of Messages — you can see the status, but only Alex can flip it), and permanently deleting a client record.

label: The site or the admin panel won't load at all
content:
If vero.photography or the admin panel at /admin won't open, nothing inside the panel can fix it — the site runs on Vercel, and all of that is Alex's. Before messaging him, two cheap checks: open the site on your phone using mobile data instead of wi-fi, and try a different browser. If it works in either, the problem is on your end, not the site.

If it fails everywhere, message Alex with the time and the exact words on your screen. What you see tells him where to look:

- A completely blank white page — the site itself didn't load. Hosting. Alex's.
- "Could not reach the server." on the sign-in screen — the page loaded but the server didn't answer. Alex's.
- "Server error (500)" — the server answered but something behind it is broken, usually the database. Alex's.
- "Admin is not configured." — a setting is missing on the server. Alex's.
- "Incorrect email or password" — nothing is broken. That's just the sign-in.

That last one is worth handling yourself before you message anyone. The email field remembers the last address used on that browser, so check it's actually yours — if it isn't, tap "Sign in as different user" under the "Welcome back" line to clear it, then type both fields fresh. There is no lockout and no penalty for trying again: a wrong attempt is deliberately slowed by about three-quarters of a second, and that's the whole of it — it never gets slower, and you are never locked out. Retry as many times as you need.

label: A client says they can't get into their gallery
content:
LABEL: A client says they can't get into their gallery

INSTRUCTION: Most causes you can fix yourself in a minute — one you can't. Open Clients (Клиенты) and tap the client to open their detail page, then work down this list in order.

1. Photo Gallery section — is the Google Drive folder link filled in? If it's empty, that's the whole problem: the client's password works but they see "Your photos are not ready yet." Paste the Drive share URL, then click the Save button that appears next to the field. Nothing in this panel saves until you press Save.

2. Delivery Status — if it reads Expired (Истекла), STOP. The gallery's hosting window ran out. The client gets "This gallery has expired," and there is no button in the panel that extends it — the Enable toggle and the password won't help, because Access will still say Enabled. Ask Alex to reopen it.

3. Gallery Pass section — Access (Доступ) must read Enabled (Включён). If it says Disabled (Отключён), tap Enable (Включить); that one saves on tap.

4. Compare the Password shown in Gallery Pass with what you actually sent them. To change it: type the new value, then click Save. If you get "That gallery password is already in use," another client already has it — pick something different.

5. Once the Drive link is set, a "Preview Client Gallery" (Посмотреть глазами клиента) button appears. Tap it — it opens the client's exact link in a new tab and logs itself in, so you see precisely what they see. Your admin session stays open in the original tab.

For a full portal client (they log in with email + password, not a gallery password), scroll to the Account section:
- Status "Invite pending" or "No account" means they never finished setup — tap Resend Invite (Отправить приглашение снова) to send a fresh invite email.
- Status "Account active" but they lost the password — tap Set Password (Задать пароль), type a new one (at least 6 characters), press Save, and tell them what it is. They can change it themselves once they're in.

REQUIRES ALEX: only for an expired gallery (step 2). Everything else is yours.

label: The client's gallery opens but shows no photos
content:
LABEL: The client's gallery opens but shows no photos

INSTRUCTION: First reproduce it yourself — go to Admin → Clients, open the client, and in the "Photo Gallery" section click "Preview Client Gallery". That button opens exactly what a client sees at /portal/pass, so you're looking at the real thing instead of guessing. Then match what you see:

1. "Your photos are not ready yet. Check back soon!" (or, if the client logs in with their email and password instead of a gallery password, "Your gallery will appear here once Veronika delivers your photos.") — no Drive folder is saved on the record. Paste the folder's share URL into the "Google Drive URL" field in the Photo Gallery section, save, then click Preview Client Gallery again. Note: the email-and-password version of this message can ALSO mean the folder is saved but the site found no photos in it, so if the field already has a link, treat it as case 2.

2. The gallery loads but is empty, with no message at all — the link works and the site could read the folder, it just didn't find photos. In Drive, check that the photos are sitting directly in that folder, or in subfolders one level down. Photos buried two levels deep (e.g. Wedding → Bride → Hair) are not picked up. Also check the files are real photos or videos, not PDFs or documents.

3. "Could not load photo previews — use 'View in Drive' below." — the site couldn't read that folder at all. In order of likelihood: (a) the saved link isn't the folder you think it is — a link to a single file, or an old/stale URL. Open the folder in Drive, copy the URL from the browser's address bar, paste it back into "Google Drive URL", save, and preview again. (b) The folder isn't inside the parent folder you shared with the website, so the site has no access — move it in, or share that folder the same way. (c) If the link is definitely the right folder and it is in the shared parent, send it to Alex — Drive access runs on a credential he manages.

If the client can't get IN at all rather than seeing an empty gallery, that's a different problem: check that Gallery Pass is enabled on the client's record, and look at the expiry — an expired gallery shows "This gallery has expired."

Everything above is yours to do; nothing here needs Alex except case 3(c).

REQUIRES ALEX: false

label: A client's gallery says it has expired
content:
A client's gallery says it has expired

That is the retention clock running out, not a broken link. It only comes from the password page (/portal/pass), so it is the shared gallery link that stopped working — a client who logs in at /portal with their own email and password is not affected.

Where to see it: open the client from Clients. In the Photo Gallery section the delivery status shows a green "Delivered {date}" badge next to either "{n} days remaining" (which turns orange in the final week) or "Expired". In the Clients list the same client shows a plain grey "Expired" badge instead of the green one.

There is no control anywhere in the panel that pushes the expiry date out. The date is set once, when the gallery is first delivered — for a Gallery Only client that happens the moment you create it with a Drive link, using the "Retention (months)" box on the new-gallery form (so there was never a button for it); for a full-portal client it happens when you press "Mark as Delivered", and that button is gone afterwards. Editing the client's fields will not help either: the expiry date is not one of the editable fields.

Two ways forward:

1. Extend the existing gallery — message Alex with the client's name and how much longer they need. It is a quick change on his side, and it keeps the client's current password working.

2. Re-share it yourself, today — Clients, "New", then "Gallery Only". Paste the same Google Drive folder URL, set "Retention (months)" to how long you want it live, and keep the auto-filled gallery password (the panel refuses a password that is already in use, so it will be a new one). If you fill in the client's email, they are automatically sent a fresh "your photos are ready" email with a one-click link. Note the old expired entry stays in your Clients list — deleting clients is Alex-only — so tell him to clean it up when he gets a chance.

label: Emails aren't arriving
content:
Split this into "one person" versus "nobody."

ONE CLIENT DIDN'T GET SOMETHING. First open their page and check the Client Email field in the Details section — you can edit it in place and it saves immediately. Then it depends which email is missing:

- Their invite (they never finished setting up their portal): scroll to the Account section. If the status badge says "Invite pending" you'll see a "Resend Invite" button — tap it. It generates a fresh 14-day link and emails it. If the send fails you'll get a red error right there, so no news is good news. The Account section only exists on full client portals (contract + login), not on gallery-only ones.
- They already set a password and are locked out: there's no Resend Invite button for them (by design). Use "Set Password" in the same Account section — type a temporary password of at least 6 characters, save, and tell them to sign in at /portal with their email and that password.
- Their "your photos are ready" email: there is no re-send button for this one. That email goes out once, at the moment you tap "Mark as Delivered," and the button disappears afterwards. So send the link yourself: for a gallery-only client, use "Preview Client Gallery" in the Photo Gallery section — it opens the exact page they get, with the password already in the URL — and copy that address out of your browser bar; the password itself is also shown in the Gallery Pass section. For a full portal client, just tell them to sign in at /portal, and use Set Password if they've lost theirs.

Worth knowing: marking a gallery delivered succeeds even when the email fails, so a green "Delivered" badge does not prove the email landed. Always worth asking them to check spam.

NOTHING IS ARRIVING FOR ANYONE — no invites, no new-lead notifications from the contact form. Stop and message Alex. All sending runs through an email service he owns, and there is no switch or status page for it in your panel.

label: Instagram messages stopped appearing
content:
Start with the refresh icon (circular arrows) at the top right of the Messages tab — the list also reloads itself every 30 seconds, so leaving the tab open for a minute does the same thing. If messages come back, it was just a stale screen.

If they don't, check which of these you're seeing, because they're different problems and knowing which one saves Alex a lot of time:

- No new Instagram DMs at all, but website contact-form messages are still landing in the same list — the Instagram connection has dropped. Nothing in the panel can restore it.
- Instagram DMs are arriving, but your replies fail with an error, or people show up as "Instagram user 483920" with no photo instead of their real handle — the Instagram access token has expired. Also not fixable from the panel.

Either way it's Alex's to fix. The Integrations tab where the Instagram connection's health is shown only exists on his login, so there's no health readout on your side.

In the meantime, reply to people from the Instagram app on your phone so nobody is left waiting. Those replies may or may not show up in the panel afterwards depending on how the connection broke — that's expected, don't re-send them here.

When you message Alex, the useful details are: roughly when the last Instagram DM you did see came in, whether website/contact-form messages are still arriving, and the exact error text if a reply failed to send.
